script: Christian von Koenigsegg was 22 years old and had no engineering degree, no factory, no investors, and no experience building cars when he decided in 1994 to start a supercar company in Sweden. Sweden had no history of supercars. Ferrari was in Italy, Lamborghini was in Italy, Porsche was in Germany. His friends told him it was an absurd idea. He started anyway, working out of a small facility outside Angelholm, assembling a team of engineers who believed in him for reasons that weren't entirely clear. The first car took 6 years to complete. In 2002, the CC8S became the first Koenigsegg delivered to a customer. It produced more horsepower per liter than any production car ever built. Authorities immediately tried to classify it as too dangerous to register on public roads. Koenigsegg fought and won. The cars kept getting faster. In 2017, the Agera RS set the production car land speed record at 277.9 miles per hour on a closed Nevada highway. The Jesko Absolut, released in 2020, is theoretically capable of 330 miles per hour, a number no production car has ever reached. The factory in Angelholm produces around 20 cars per year.
